Use it to see which Blueprint the ID belongs to. bp-<X>_time_submitted When the participant submitted the donation for this Blueprint. bp-<X>_consent True if the participant consented to donate this Blueprint's data, False if not. bp-<X>_extraction_state DATA_EXTRACTED: data was extracted. NOT_ATTEMPTED: the participant reached the data donation step but didn't upload a file. FAILED: the upload or extraction failed. NO_DATA_EXTRACTED: the Extraction Rules removed all entries. bp-<X>_n_data_entries The number of entries in the donation. For some data structures, the actual number may be higher.

Test runs

Participants who used the test link are included and marked with is_test_case = True. Exclude them before you analyze the data. For exceptions, see Test and Launch.

docs.title: Download Questionnaire Responses
docs.text:
In the Data Center section of the Project Hub, click Download CSV next to the questionnaire responses.

The file has one row per participant and one column per question or item, named after its Variable Name (see Questionnaire Configuration).

The responses use these codes for missing values:

  • -77: The question or item wasn't shown because of a filter.
  • -99: The participant saw the question or item but didn't answer it.

The questionnaire_complete column is true if the participant submitted the last page of the questionnaire, and false if they stopped partway through.

docs.title: Download Through the API
docs.text:
1. In the Data Center section of the Project Hub, click Manage Remote Access.
  2. Create an API token.
  3. Use the token in your script. For the available endpoints and examples, see APIs.

Share data access carefully

Only the researcher who created a project can open it in DDM. To give colleagues access to the data, you can share an API token instead. Anyone with the token can download all collected data, so share it only with people who are allowed to see the data, and set a short expiration date.

docs.title: Participation Statistics
docs.text:
The Participation Statistics currently display the following information. Test runs made through the project's Test Link are excluded from all of these:

  • At least one donated file: The number of participants who successfully donated at least one file.
  • Donated Files: The number of successfully donated files. A "status by blueprint" link opens a breakdown of donation outcomes per Blueprint.
  • Started: The number of participants that started the study.
  • Completed: The number of participants that reached the debriefing page of the study.
  • Completion Rate: The number of completed divided by the number of started participations.
  • Avg. Time to Complete: The average time it took completed participants to go from starting the study to reaching the debriefing page.

docs.title: Project Logs
docs.text:
The project logs help you spot problems while your study is running, for example participants whose files DDM can't read, or a Blueprint that doesn't match the platform's current export. Check them after you launch your project and regularly while it runs.

To open them, go to the Project Hub and click Project Logs.

There are two logs:

  • The Exception Log lists problems that occurred during participation.
  • The Event Log lists actions on the project, such as data downloads and deletions.

docs.title: Exception Log
docs.text:
Each entry shows:

  • When the problem occurred.
  • The type of problem (see below).
  • The participant and Blueprint concerned, if any.
  • Whether it occurred in the participant's browser (client side) or on the server (server side).
  • A message with details.

docs.title: Problems in the Participant's Browser
docs.text:
These problems occur while DDM processes the uploaded file in the participant's browser.

Problems with the participant's file. Usually, the participant uploaded the wrong file. If many participants are affected, the platform may have changed its export, or your instructions may be unclear.

Code Meaning INVALID_ZIP The Uploader expects a ZIP file, but the participant uploaded a different file type. ZIP_READ_FAIL The ZIP file couldn't be read. The message contains the error and, for a nested ZIP file, its path and depth. NO_FILE_MATCH The ZIP file doesn't contain a file that matches the Blueprint's File paths. STRING_CONVERSION_ERROR The file's content couldn't be read as text. PARSING_ERROR The file couldn't be read in the expected format (JSON, CSV, or TXT). EXTRACTION_ROOT_NOT_FOUND The file doesn't contain the Blueprint's Extraction Root. NESTED_PATH_NOT_FOUND The file doesn't contain the Blueprint's Nested loop path.

Problems with your configuration. Fix these in the Blueprint.

Code Meaning INVALID_REGEX A regular expression in File paths isn't valid. INVALID_FIELD_REGEX A regular expression in a field name isn't valid. NO_FIELDS_TO_EXTRACT No field has Keep in donation enabled. In older logs, this is called NO_EXTRACTION_RULES. MORE_THAN_ONE_KEY_MATCH More than one field in the file matches a field's Expected name. Make the name or regular expression more specific.

Unexpected problems. If these occur, please check carefully and consider reporting an issue.

Code Meaning FILE_PROCESSING_FAIL_GENERAL An unexpected error occurred while processing the file. UNSUPPORTED_BP_FORMAT The Blueprint's file format isn't supported.

docs.title: Extraction Summaries
docs.text:
These entries aren't problems. DDM writes them once per Blueprint every time it processes a file successfully. Use them to check whether your Blueprint extracts what you expect.

Code Contains EXTRACTION_STATS Counts of the extraction: rows in total (nRowsTotal), rows with a missing field (nRowsMissingField), rows removed by Extraction Rules (nRowsFilteredOut), and which fields weren't found how often (noKeyMatches). With a Nested loop path, also the number of sub-entries (nNestedRowsTotal) and of sub-entries skipped because of Nested expected fields (nNestedRowsMissingField). EXTRACTION_LOG How often each Extraction Rule was applied, by rule ID. EXTRACTED_FIELDS_MAP Which field in the file was matched to which Expected name. Useful if you use regular expressions.

For example, if nRowsFilteredOut is close to nRowsTotal for most participants, your Extraction Rules may remove more than intended.

docs.title: Problems on the Server
docs.text:
Server-side problems don't have codes. Their message starts with where they occurred:

  • Data Donation Processing Exception: The server couldn't process a donation, for example because the uploaded data was incomplete or invalid.
  • Questionnaire Post Exception: The server couldn't save questionnaire responses, for example because a response didn't match the question's options.

Problems in the questionnaire are logged only on the server.

docs.title: Event Log
docs.text:
The Event Log records:

  • Deleted API tokens.
  • API requests that failed authentication or were denied.
  • Data downloads, whether successful, failed, or denied.
  • Data deletions, whether successful, failed, or denied.
  • Deletions of individual participants, whether successful, failed, or denied.
  • Problems in the participant's browser that couldn't be assigned to a participant, for example because their session had expired.

docs.title: Data Collection Configuration
docs.text:
Configure what participants see and do, step by step. Participants go through the steps in this order:

  1. Briefing Page: Introduces your study when participants open the link.
  2. Data Donation: Participants upload their data, review it, and decide what to donate. You define which files you expect, which data is extracted, and the instructions participants follow.
  3. Questionnaire (optional): Questions shown after the donation, which can refer to the donated data.
  4. Debriefing Page: The last page, for example to thank participants or send them on to a follow-up survey.

The order is fixed

You can't change the order of the steps or skip the briefing and debriefing pages. Only the questionnaire is optional.

To ask questions before the donation, use an external survey tool (for example, SoSciSurvey or Qualtrics) first and send participants on to DDM with their ID in the link. See URL Parameter Extraction.

To configure a step, open the Project Hub and select it under Data Collection Configuration:

docs.title: Briefing Page
docs.text: The briefing page is the first part of your project and is used to onboard participants and brief them about your project and the steps ahead. Additionally, you can obtain explicit consent for the general study participation by requiring participants to confirm that they have read and agree with the provided information.

docs.title: Participants' Perspective
docs.text: To the participants, the briefing page will look something like this:

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text:
You can access the configuration options for the briefing page in Project Hub > Data Collection Configuration > Briefing. To configure the briefing page, you have the following options.

Settings

Briefing Text

Text displayed to participants on the briefing page.

Tip

In the briefing text, you can make use of dynamic template functionalities. You can read more about how to use dynamic templates here.

Briefing Consent Mandatory

If enabled, participants will have to provide explicit participation consent before they can advance to the data donation. If a participant does indicate that they do not consent, they will be redirected to the debriefing page.

Response Consent

The label displayed to participants to indicate consent.

Response Non-Consent

The label displayed to participants to reject consent.

docs.title: Debriefing Page
docs.text: The debriefing page is the last page participants see. Use it to thank participants, explain the purpose of the study, and, if needed, send them on to the next part of your study, such as a follow-up survey.

docs.title: Participants' Perspective
docs.text: To show a button that takes participants to another website, such as your survey, see General Project Settings → Redirect Configuration.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Open the Project Hub and go to Data Collection Configuration → Debriefing.

Settings

Debriefing text

The text shown on the debriefing page.

docs.title: Show Different Texts to Different Participants
docs.text:
You can adapt the debriefing text to what happened during participation, for example to tell participants whose files couldn't be processed that they aren't eligible for a reward.

To do this, add conditions to the text. A condition starts with {% if … %}, can have alternatives ({% elif … %}, {% else %}), and ends with {% endif %}. DDM shows only the text of the first condition that applies:

{% if donation_info.n_success > 0 %}
    Thank you very much for participating in our study. With your data donation, you made a
    great contribution to our research.
{% elif donation_info.n_no_data_extracted > 0 %}
    Thank you for your time. Unfortunately, no data could be extracted from your upload, so
    you aren't eligible for the participation reward.
{% else %}
    Thank you for your time.
{% endif %}

In this example:

  • Participants who donated at least some data see the first text.
  • Participants who donated nothing, and from whose upload no data could be extracted, see the second text.
  • Everyone else, for example participants who declined to donate, sees the third text.

For all donation_info values and other variables, see Template Rendering → Available Variables.

docs.title: Data Donation Configuration
docs.text:
You configure the data donation step with three building blocks:

  • Uploaders: An Uploader is an upload form for one file, either a single file or a ZIP file. If participants should donate data from several platforms, create one Uploader per platform.
  • Instructions: Each Uploader can have instructions that show participants how to request and download the file from the platform.
  • Blueprints: A Blueprint defines which data DDM extracts from the uploaded file. Each Uploader has one or more Blueprints, for example one for the watch history and one for the search history in the same YouTube export.

To configure the data donation step, open the Project Hub and, under Data Collection Configuration, click Data Donation:

docs.title: Uploader Configuration
docs.text:
Settings

Upload Type

Single file if participants upload one file, such as a CSV or JSON file. Zip file if they upload a ZIP file, as most platforms provide.

Name

Internal name of the Uploader. Participants don't see it. Must be unique within the project.

Extract nested zip files

If enabled, DDM also opens ZIP files inside the uploaded ZIP file, so that Blueprints can extract data from the files they contain.

In the file paths of a Blueprint, files inside a nested ZIP file include the ZIP file's name. For example, inner.json inside nested.zip has the path nested.zip/inner.json.

Extraction depth

How many levels of nested ZIP files DDM opens. With 1, DDM opens ZIP files inside the uploaded ZIP file, but not ZIP files inside those. With 0, DDM opens only the uploaded ZIP file.

Display name

The Uploader's name in the header of the upload form, as participants see it, for example "YouTube".

Display position

If you use several Uploaders, the order in which they're shown. Uploaders with a lower number are shown first.

All-in-one consent

By default, participants consent separately to the data of each Blueprint. With all-in-one consent, they consent once to all extracted data, at the bottom of the page.

All-in-one consent disabled:

All-in-one consent enabled:

docs.title: Instruction Configuration
docs.text:
After you create an Uploader, you can add instructions to it. Instructions consist of one or more pages, which participants go through with Next and Back buttons. If an Uploader has no instructions, participants go straight to the upload form.

Settings

Text

The text of the instruction page. You can also upload and add images or GIFs, for example screenshots that show where to request the data on the platform.

Let participants continue later

Requesting data from a platform can take hours or days. To let participants return later, show them their participant ID with the variable {{ participant_id }}. It appears as a code like IPI2wHDWrHODDRKuo8zo101S. See Continuation.

Page number

The position of the page in the instructions.

docs.title: Blueprint Configuration
docs.text:
A Blueprint processes the uploaded file in these steps:

  1. Find the file: In a ZIP file, find the file that matches the File paths.
  2. Check the file: Check that it has the expected format and contains the Expected fields.
  3. Select the fields: Keep only the Relevant Fields.
  4. Filter and clean: Apply the Extraction Rules, for example to remove entries before a certain date or to anonymize email addresses.

Participants then review the result before they donate it.

docs.title: General Settings
docs.text:
Settings

Name

Internal name of the Blueprint. Participants don't see it.

Associated Uploader

The Uploader whose file this Blueprint processes.

docs.title: Display Settings
docs.text:
Settings

Display name

The name participants see above the extracted data. Choose a name that describes the data, for example "Watch History" or "Liked Posts".

Description

Optional. Describes the extracted data for participants, for example "The date you watched each video and the link to the video".

Display order

The order of the Blueprints on the page. Blueprints with a lower number are shown first. Blueprints with the same number are shown in the order they were created.

docs.title: Data Extraction Configuration
docs.text:
Settings

File paths

Only needed if the Uploader expects a ZIP file. The path of the file inside the ZIP file. For example, if some_data.json is at the top level of the ZIP file, enter some_data.json.

Paths are matched from the end: data.json matches both root/data.json and root/some-folder/data.json. If a path matches more than one file, DDM extracts data from all of them, so make the path as specific as possible.

You can add several paths, for example if the file name differs between platform languages. DDM tries them in order, lowest number first: the first path with at least one match is used (and all files matching it are extracted), and any later paths are ignored.

Using regular expressions in file paths

A regular expression (regex) is a pattern that matches several possible texts. For an introduction, see Regular expressions on MDN. To test a pattern, use regex101 with the "ECMAScript (JavaScript)" flavor.

Examples:

  • ^MyActivities\.json$: A file named MyActivities.json at the top level of the ZIP file.
  • ^SpecificFolder/MyActivities\.json$: A file named MyActivities.json in the folder SpecificFolder at the top level.
  • .*/MyActivities\.json$: A file named MyActivities.json in any folder.
  • ^(MyActivities|MeineAktivitäten|MieAttivita)\.json$: A file at the top level named MyActivities.json, MeineAktivitäten.json, or MieAttivita.json, for example the same file in different platform languages.

Patterns are case-sensitive: myactivities\.json doesn't match MyActivities.json. To allow both spellings, list them in the pattern, for example [Mm]y[Aa]ctivities\.json.

For files inside nested ZIP files, see Extract nested zip files.

Expected File Format

The format of the file: JSON, CSV, or TXT.

Expected fields

The fields the file must contain. If the file doesn't contain all of them, DDM extracts nothing from it. Put each field name in double quotes and separate them with commas, for example "Field A", "Field B".

Expected fields use regex matching

Enable this if Expected fields contains regular expressions instead of exact field names. Like all regular expressions in DDM, they're case-sensitive.

Array join separator

Some fields contain several values, for example the lines of a message. DDM combines them into one text, separated by this character. The default, \n, puts each value on its own line: ["A", "B"] becomes A and B on two lines.

docs.title: JSON-Specific Settings
docs.text:
Settings

Extraction Root

Where in the file the data to extract is. Leave it empty if the data is at the top level of the file. If the data is nested inside other fields, enter the path to it, with field names separated by dots.

For example, to extract the names and dates of real_friends from this file, enter friends.real_friends:

{
  "friends": {
    "real_friends": [{"name": "Alice", "date": "2024-01-01"}],
    "fake_friends": [{"name": "Bob", "date": "2024-02-01"}]
  }
}

docs.title: Nested Loop Settings
docs.text:
Sometimes each entry in a file contains a list of sub-entries that you want as separate rows. For example, a ChatGPT export has one entry per conversation, and each conversation contains a list of messages:

[
  {
    "conversation_id": "conv-1",
    "title": "Weekend Trip Ideas",
    "mapping": [
      {"message": {"author": "user", "content": "Where should we go this weekend?"}},
      {"message": {"author": "assistant", "content": "How about a hike near the lake?"}}
    ]
  },
  {
    "conversation_id": "conv-2",
    "title": "Restaurant Ideas",
    "mapping": [
      {"message": {"author": "assistant", "content": "some content 2"}}
    ]
  }
]

By default, DDM extracts one row per conversation and can't reach the individual messages. With Nested loop path set to mapping, DDM creates one row per message and repeats the conversation's fields in each row:

conversation_id title author content conv-1 Weekend Trip Ideas user Where should we go this weekend? conv-1 Weekend Trip Ideas assistant How about a hike near the lake? conv-2 Restaurant Ideas assistant some content 2

This also works if mapping is an object instead of a list, for example "mapping": {"some_uuid": {"message": {...}}}. DDM then ignores the keys (some_uuid) and uses the values.

All settings in this section apply only to JSON Blueprints with a Nested loop path.

Settings

Nested loop path

The field that contains the sub-entries, for example mapping. For a field inside another field, separate the names with dots, for example data.mapping. Leave it empty if you don't need it.

To extract fields of the sub-entries, add them as Relevant Fields with the scope Nested level, for example message.author and message.content.

Nested expected fields

Like Expected fields, but checked for each sub-entry. DDM skips sub-entries that don't contain all of these fields and still processes the rest of the entry. Put each field name in double quotes and separate them with commas, for example "Field A", "Field B".

Nested expected fields use regex matching

Enable this if Nested expected fields contains regular expressions.

Group entries by parent item

By default, participants see all sub-entries (for example, all messages from all conversations) in one list. If enabled, they see them grouped by entry, for example all messages of a conversation together, with the conversation's title shown once above them.

Allow item exclusion

If enabled, participants can remove individual entries, for example a single conversation, before they donate. Otherwise, they can only donate or decline all data of the Blueprint. Requires Group entries by parent item.

docs.title: CSV-Specific Settings
docs.text:
Settings

CSV Delimiter

The character that separates values in the file, for example ,, ;, or \t (tab). If you leave it empty, DDM detects it from the file.

docs.title: TXT-Specific Settings
docs.text:
For example, for this file:

Datum: 2026-04-01 14:09:16 UTC
Link: https://example.com/video/1

Datum: 2026-04-02 15:30:48 UTC
Link: https://example.com/video/2

set Record/entry separator to (blank line), Field separator to (line break), and Key-value separator to :. DDM extracts two entries, each with the fields Datum and Link.

Entering line breaks

In the separator settings, type (a backslash followed by "n") for a line break and for a blank line. Don't paste an actual line break into the field.

Settings

Record/entry separator

What separates one entry from the next, for example for a blank line or for a line break.

Field separator

What separates the fields within an entry, for example if each field is on its own line.

Key-value separator

What separates a field's name from its value, for example : in Name: John or = in name=John.

Skip header lines

How many lines to skip at the start of the file, for example a title or metadata.

Skip footer lines

How many lines to skip at the end of the file, for example a summary.

Ignore blank lines

If enabled, DDM ignores empty lines within an entry instead of treating them as part of a field.

Trim whitespace

If enabled, DDM removes spaces at the start and end of each entry and each field.

docs.title: Relevant Fields
docs.text:
Once DDM has found and checked the file, it extracts only the fields you define here. You can also rename fields, for example to get the same column name for files in different platform languages.

Settings

Scope

Root level (the default) reads the field from the entry. Nested level reads it from a sub-entry (see Nested Loop Settings), for example message.author in the ChatGPT example. Nested level is only available for JSON Blueprints with a Nested loop path.

Expected name

The field's name in the file, or a regular expression if Match regex is enabled, for example to match the same field in different platform languages. Without regex, you can reach a field inside another field with dots, for example message.author.role.

Match regex

Enable this if Expected name is a regular expression instead of an exact name.

Rename to

Optional. The field's name in the extracted data. If empty, DDM uses the Expected name. Useful with regular expressions, so the column has a predictable name.

Keep in donation

If enabled, the field is part of the donated data. If disabled, you can still use the field in Extraction Rules (for example, to filter by date) without collecting it.

docs.title: Extraction Rules
docs.text:
Extraction Rules filter and clean the extracted data. DDM applies them one after another, in the order you define. Each rule either removes entries that meet a condition or changes the text of a field.

Info

Rules don't decide which fields are kept; Keep in donation does (see Relevant Fields). You only need rules to filter or change data.

Settings

Execution Order

The order in which the rules are applied. Rules with a lower number are applied first.

Name

Internal name of the rule. It's not the name of the field.

Field

The field the rule checks or changes. Must match the field's Expected name or, if set, its Rename to value.

Extraction Operator

What the rule does. See Operators.

Comparison Value

The value or regular expression the field is compared with.

Replacement Value

Only for Replace match (regex): the text that replaces the matching parts.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Operators that remove entries. Each of these operators removes every entry for which the condition is true.

Extraction Operator Removes an entry if the field… Works with Equal (==) equals the comparison value. Text, numbers, dates1 Not Equal (!=) doesn't equal the comparison value. Text, numbers, dates1 Greater than (>) is greater than the comparison value. Numbers, dates1 Smaller than (<) is smaller than the comparison value. Numbers, dates1 Greater than or equal (>=) is greater than or equal to the comparison value. Numbers, dates1 Smaller than or equal (<=) is smaller than or equal to the comparison value. Numbers, dates1 Delete row when match (regex) matches the regular expression. Any value (treated as text)

For the greater/smaller operators, entries whose field contains text are kept.

Operators that change text.

Extraction Operator What it does Works with Delete match (regex) Deletes the parts of the field that match the regular expression. Any value (treated as text) Replace match (regex) Replaces the parts of the field that match the regular expression with the Replacement Value. Any value (treated as text)

Examples:

  • Delete match (regex) with ^Watched turns Watched video XY into video XY.
  • Replace match (regex) with [\w.-]+@([\w-]+\.)+[\w-]{2,} and the replacement value _anonymized_ turns some text email@address.com into some text _anonymized_.
  • Delete row when match (regex) with ^Watched removes every entry whose field starts with Watched.

docs.title: Backup Blueprints (Advanced)
docs.text:
A backup Blueprint is a fallback: if a Blueprint can't extract data from a participant's file, for example because the platform changed its export format, DDM tries the backup instead. Participants see the result of whichever Blueprint succeeds. If the main Blueprint succeeds, DDM doesn't use the backups.

For example, Watch History expects the current JSON export. A second Blueprint, Watch History (old format), expects the TXT export that the platform used before, with Backup for set to Watch History. If a participant uploads an old export, DDM uses the backup.

Settings

Backup for

The Blueprint that this Blueprint is a backup for. Leave it empty if this isn't a backup. You can only choose Blueprints of the same Uploader. A backup can't have its own backup.

Backup priority

If a Blueprint has several backups, DDM tries the one with the lowest number first.

docs.title: Advanced Options
docs.text:
Under Advanced Options, you can edit the texts of the upload form, such as button labels and messages, for all Uploaders of the project.

  1. DDM recognizes dates in ISO, RFC 2822, or HTTP format, for example 2026-04-01T14:09:16Z, but only if the field and the comparison value use the same format. Otherwise, it compares them as text. ↩↩↩↩↩↩

docs.title: Data Donation
docs.text:
On the data donation page, participants upload their data, review it, and decide whether to donate it. The page follows the briefing page.

Donated data stays on the participant's device until they consent

DDM checks, extracts, and filters the uploaded data in the participant's browser. The content of the donation is sent to your server only after the participant reviews it and clicks Transmit data.

Before consent, DDM may send technical information about the uploaded file, such as its file structure, to help you diagnose problems (see Project Logs).

docs.title: Participants' Perspective
docs.text:
Participants go through three steps:

  1. Instructions: Participants read how to request and download their data from the platform.

  2. Upload: Participants upload the file they received from the platform.

  3. Review and consent: Participants see the data that DDM extracted from their file and decide whether to donate it.

docs.title: Researchers' Perspective
docs.text:
Between upload and review, DDM processes the file according to the rules you define:

  1. Check the file: DDM verifies that the participant uploaded the expected file.
  2. Extract and filter: DDM keeps only the data your extraction rules ask for and removes everything else.

Participants then review only this extracted data, so they know exactly what they donate.

To set up the instructions and extraction rules, see Data Donation Configuration.

docs.title: Questionnaire Configuration
docs.text: This page describes the settings for questions and their items, scales, and filters. To configure the questionnaire, open the Project Hub and, under Data Collection Configuration, click Questionnaire.

docs.title: Question Types
docs.text:
• Single Choice Question: Participants choose one answer.

  • Multi Choice Question: Participants choose one or more answers.

  • Matrix Question: Several items rated on the same scale.

  • Semantic Differential: Several items rated on a scale between two opposite terms.

  • Open Question: Participants answer in their own words.

  • Text Block: Text without a question, for example an introduction to the next page.

docs.title: General Settings
docs.text:
These settings are available for all question types.

Settings

Name

Internal name of the question. Participants don't see it.

Blueprint

Whether the question is shown to everyone or depends on a Blueprint:

  • General questions are shown to all participants, whether or not they donated data.
  • Questions linked to a Blueprint are shown only to participants for whom that Blueprint extracted data. If no data was extracted, because the extraction failed, wasn't attempted, or the Extraction Rules removed all entries, the question isn't shown.

Questions linked to a Blueprint can refer to the donated data. See Data Integration.

Page

The number of the page the question is shown on.

Index

The order of the questions on the same page. Questions with a lower number are shown first.

Variable Name

The question's column name in the data download. For questions with items, each item gets its own column, named <variable name>-<item value>. For example, the item with the value 2 in the question media_use becomes media_use-2.

Text

The question text that participants see.

Requirement level

Whether participants must answer the question:

  • Not required: Participants can skip the question.
  • Soft: If participants skip the question, they see a reminder once. They can then continue without answering.
  • Hard: Participants can't continue without answering.

Randomize items

If enabled, the items of the question are shown in random order. To randomize only some items, use Randomize on the items instead.

docs.title: Open Question
docs.text:
Settings

Input type

What participants can enter: text (anything, the default), number (only numbers), or email (only valid email addresses).

Minimum input length

The minimum number of characters. If empty, there's no minimum.

Maximum input length

The maximum number of characters. If empty, there's no maximum.

Minimum input value

Only for the input type number: the smallest number allowed. If empty, there's no minimum.

Maximum input value

Only for the input type number: the largest number allowed. If empty, there's no maximum.

Restrictions are only hints

If participants enter something that doesn't meet the input type or limits, they see a hint, but they can still continue. Your data can therefore contain values outside these limits, so check them when you analyze the data.

Display

Only for the input type text: small (a one-line field, the default) or a larger field with several lines.

Multi item response

If enabled, you can add items, and participants answer each item in its own field. If disabled, the question has one field below the question text.

docs.title: Matrix Question
docs.text:
Settings

Show scale headings

Whether the Heading label of each scale point is shown above the scale.

docs.title: Question Items
docs.text:
Single Choice Questions, Multi Choice Questions, Matrix Questions, and Semantic Differentials consist of items: the answer options or the statements that participants rate.

Settings

Index

The order of the items. Items with a lower number are shown first.

Label

The item's text. For Semantic Differentials, the term on the left side of the scale. Supports basic formatting.

Label Right

Only for Semantic Differentials: the term on the right side of the scale. Supports basic formatting.

Value

Identifies the item in the data download. For Single Choice Questions, the value of the selected item is saved. For the other question types, the value is part of the item's column name (see Variable Name under General Settings).

Randomize

If enabled for some items, only those items swap places randomly. The others stay in the position set by their Index.

Delete

Deletes the item when you click Save.

docs.title: Scale Configuration
docs.text:
For Matrix Questions and Semantic Differentials, participants rate each item on a scale.

Settings

Index

The order of the scale points. Scale points with a lower number are shown first.

Input label

The text in the scale point's button. Supports basic formatting.

Long labels

If labels are long or the scale has many points, mark where a word may break with ­. For example, un­decided is shown as "undecided" if it fits, and otherwise as "un-" at the end of one line and "decided" on the next.

Heading label

Only for Matrix Questions: the text above the scale point. Supports basic formatting.

Value

The value saved in the data download when a participant selects this scale point.

Secondary point

If enabled, the scale point is shown separately from the main scale, for example for a "Don't know" option.

Delete

Deletes the scale point when you click Save.

docs.title: Formatting Labels
docs.text:
Label, Label Right, Input label, and Heading label support basic HTML formatting:

  • <b> or <strong> for bold, <i> or <em> for italics, and <u> for underlined text.
  • <sub> and <sup> for subscript and superscript.
  • <br> for a line break.
  • <span class="…"> to apply one of the available Bootstrap CSS classes, for example <span class="text-muted">.

DDM removes all other HTML, including style attributes, when you save. You don't get an error message.

docs.title: Filter Configuration
docs.text:
Filters hide questions or items depending on earlier answers, URL parameters, participant information, or the donation. For example, you can ask a follow-up question only to participants who answered "Yes" to a previous question.

DDM hides the question or item if the filter conditions are met. Hidden questions and items are coded as -77 in the data download.

If all items of a question are hidden, the question is hidden. If all questions on a page are hidden, participants skip the page.

Settings

Index

The order of the conditions. Conditions with a lower number come first.

Combinator

How a condition combines with the previous one: AND (both must be met) or OR (at least one must be met). The first condition's combinator is ignored.

AND takes precedence over OR. For example, A OR B AND C OR D means A OR (B AND C) OR D.

Comparison Source

What the condition checks:

  • An earlier answer. For Single Choice Questions and Open Questions, the whole question. For Multi Choice Questions, Matrix Questions, Semantic Differentials, and Open Questions with Multi item response, the individual items. Text Blocks can't be used, and a question can't refer to itself.
  • A URL parameter, if URL Parameter Extraction is enabled.
  • Participant information: participant ID, start time, end time, whether the participant completed the study, and briefing consent (if enabled).
  • Donation information: for example, the number of successful or failed donations. See Template Rendering → Available Variables.

Comparison Operator

How the source is compared with the Comparison Value: Equal (==), Not Equal (!=), Greater than (>), Smaller than (<), Greater than or equal (>=), Smaller than or equal (<=), Contains, or Does not Contain.

For Open Questions with an input type other than number, only Equal (==), Not Equal (!=), Contains, and Does not Contain are available.

Comparison Value

The value the source is compared with.

Delete

Deletes the condition when you click Save.

docs.title: Data Integration
docs.text:
Questions linked to a Blueprint can include the participant's donated data. For example, you can ask about a specific video from the participant's watch history:

Why did you watch "How to Bake Sourdough Bread"?

DDM fills in the data for each participant when the question is shown.

Note

This isn't available for projects with enhanced encryption.

docs.title: How the Donated Data Is Structured
docs.text:
In a question linked to a Blueprint, the variable donated_data contains the data that this Blueprint extracted for the participant. It's a list of entries, one per row. Each entry contains the Relevant Fields of the Blueprint, under their Rename to names if you set them.

For example, a watch-history Blueprint with the fields title and time could produce:

title time How to Bake Sourdough Bread 2026-04-02 15:30 Why are Harry's eyes blue 2026-04-01 14:09

The entries keep the order of the platform's file. Check whether the first entry is the oldest or the newest before you refer to "the last video".

docs.title: Include Data in a Question
docs.text:
Write variables in double curly braces. Use the entry's position (starting at 0) and the field name, separated by dots:

Why did you watch "{{ donated_data.0.title }}"?

To list several entries, use a loop. This example lists the first three titles:

Which of these videos do you remember?
{% for entry in donated_data %}{% if forloop.counter <= 3 %}
- {{ entry.title }}
{% endif %}{% endfor %}

You can also use the variables available in all texts, such as {{ participant_id }} and {{ url_parameter.<name> }}. For all variables and more examples, see Template Rendering.

To show or hide questions depending on the donation, use filters.

docs.title: Questionnaire
docs.text: You can add an optional questionnaire that participants fill out after the data donation. It has one or more pages, each with one or more questions.

docs.title: Question Types
docs.text:
• Single Choice Question: Participants choose one answer.
  • Multi Choice Question: Participants choose one or more answers.
  • Matrix Question: Several statements rated on the same scale, for example from "strongly disagree" to "strongly agree".
  • Semantic Differential: Several items rated on a scale between two opposite terms, for example "boring" and "exciting".
  • Open Question: Participants answer in their own words.
  • Text Block: Text without a question, for example an introduction to the next page.

To create and configure questions, see Questionnaire Configuration.

docs.title: Include Donated Data in Questions
docs.text:
Questions can refer to each participant's donated data. For example, if participants donate their YouTube watch history, you can ask about the last video they watched:

Why did you watch "How to Bake Sourdough Bread"?

DDM fills in the video title for each participant. See Data Integration.

Note

This isn't available for projects with enhanced encryption.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text: To download the responses, see Download.

docs.title: Missing Values
docs.text:
The responses use these codes:

  • -77: The question or item wasn't shown because of a filter.
  • -99: The participant saw the question or item but didn't answer it.

docs.title: Partial Responses
docs.text:
DDM saves responses as participants go through the questionnaire, not only when they submit it. If a participant stops after two of four questions, you still receive the answers to those two questions.

The questionnaire_complete column shows whether a participant submitted the last page (true) or stopped partway through (false), for example for drop-off analysis.

Mention this in your data protection statement

Participants who stop partway may assume that their answers weren't saved. Tell them in your data protection statement that answers are saved as they go.

docs.title: APIs
docs.text:
With the API, you can download data with a script instead of clicking through the Project Hub. For example, you can:

  • Download all donations, directly into R or Python.
  • Update your analysis or a monitoring dashboard automatically while the study is running.
  • Show participants a personal report based on their donated data, for example as an incentive.

The API has four endpoints:

Endpoint What it returns or does Project Overview The participants, Blueprints, and project settings. Donations The donated data. Responses The questionnaire responses. Delete Participant Deletes a participant and their data.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
1. Create an API token. In the Data Center section of the Project Hub, click Manage Remote Access and create a token. Tokens are valid for at most 90 days; after that, create a new one.

2. Find your project ID. The project ID is shown in the Overview section of the Project Hub, for example KPHn7aw7. It's not the same as the URL Identifier in the General Project Settings.

3. Build the URL. All endpoints start with your DDM server's address, the path DDM is installed under (usually /ddm), and /api/project/<project-id>. For example:

https://ddm.example.org/ddm/api/project/KPHn7aw7/overview

4. Authenticate. Send the token in the Authorization header of every request, as Token <your-token>.

Keep your token and project password secret

Anyone with the token can download all data of the project. Don't write the token or the project password into scripts that you share or put under version control. Store them in environment variables instead, as in the examples below.

docs.title: Projects with Enhanced Encryption
docs.text:
For projects with enhanced encryption, the Donations and Responses endpoints also need the project password, in the X-Project-Secret header. Without the correct password, they return the status 422. The Project Overview and Delete Participant endpoints don't need it.

In the API, projects with enhanced encryption are called super secret projects.

docs.title: Rate Limit
docs.text: Each token can make up to 100 requests per minute. Above that, the API returns the status 429. Your DDM administrator can change this limit.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
These examples download all donations of a project. They first get the participant IDs from the Project Overview endpoint and then download the donations of those participants.

PythonR 
import os
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://ddm.example.org/ddm/api/project/KPHn7aw7"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Token {os.environ['DDM_TOKEN']}"}
# For projects with enhanced encryption, also send the project password:
# HEADERS["X-Project-Secret"] = os.environ["DDM_PROJECT_PASSWORD"]

overview = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/overview", headers=HEADERS)
overview.raise_for_status()
participant_ids = [p["external_id"] for p in overview.json()["participants"]]

donations = requests.get(
    f"{BASE_URL}/donations",
    headers=HEADERS,
    params={"participants": ",".join(participant_ids)},
)
donations.raise_for_status()
data = donations.json()

library(httr2)

base_url <- "https://ddm.example.org/ddm/api/project/KPHn7aw7"
token <- Sys.getenv("DDM_TOKEN")

ddm_request <- function(path) {
  request(paste0(base_url, path)) |>
    req_headers(Authorization = paste("Token", token))
  # For projects with enhanced encryption, also add:
  # |> req_headers(`X-Project-Secret` = Sys.getenv("DDM_PROJECT_PASSWORD"))
}

overview <- ddm_request("/overview") |> req_perform() |> resp_body_json()
participant_ids <- vapply(overview$participants, \(p) p$external_id, character(1))

data <- ddm_request("/donations") |>
  req_url_query(participants = paste(participant_ids, collapse = ",")) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()

Many participants

With many participants, the URL can get too long. Request the donations in batches of, for example, 20 participants.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
All endpoints can return these errors:

Status Message Meaning 401 Authentication failed. The token is missing, invalid, or expired. 403 Permission Denied. The token is valid but not permitted to make this request. 404 Project not found. No project exists with this project ID. 429 Too many requests (see Rate Limit).

The Donations and Responses endpoints can also return:

Status Message Meaning 422 Missing or incorrect secret. The project uses enhanced encryption, and the X-Project-Secret header is missing or wrong.

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text:
Returns the participants, the Blueprints, and the project settings.

GET /api/project/<project-id>/overview

Header Required Description Authorization Yes Token <your-token>

Response:

{
    "participants": [
        {
            "external_id": "<string: participant ID>",
            "start_time": "<string: date and time (ISO 8601)>",
            "end_time": "<string: date and time (ISO 8601), or null>",
            "completed": "<boolean>",
            "url_parameter": "<object: extracted URL parameters>",
            "extra_data": "<object: additional data, for example briefing consent>",
            "current_step": "<integer: 0 = started, 1 = briefing completed, 2 = data donation completed, 3 = questionnaire completed>"
        }
    ],
    "blueprints": [
        {
            "id": "<integer: Blueprint ID>",
            "name": "<string>",
            "description": "<string or null>",
            "format": "<string: json, csv, or txt>",
            "expected_fields": "<list of strings>",
            "exp_fields_regex_matching": "<boolean>",
            "nested_expected_fields": "<list of strings>",
            "nested_exp_fields_regex_matching": "<boolean>",
            "parser_config": "<object: format-specific settings, see below>",
            "nested_display_by_root_item": "<boolean: Group entries by parent item>",
            "nested_entry_exclusion_allowed": "<boolean: Allow item exclusion>",
            "fields_to_extract": "<list of strings: fields with Keep in donation>",
            "extraction_fields": "<list: Relevant Fields, see below>",
            "file_paths": "<list of {\"path\": string, \"is_regex\": boolean}>",
            "extraction_rules": "<list: Extraction Rules, see below>",
            "is_backup": "<boolean>",
            "backup_ids": "<list of integers: IDs of this Blueprint's backups>"
        }
    ],
    "project": {
        "url_id": "<string: project ID>",
        "name": "<string>",
        "date_created": "<string: date and time (ISO 8601)>",
        "contact_information": "<string>",
        "data_protection_statement": "<string>",
        "slug": "<string: URL Identifier>",
        "url_parameter_enabled": "<boolean>",
        "expected_url_parameters": "<string>",
        "active": "<boolean>"
    },
    "metadata": {
        "n_blueprints": "<integer>",
        "n_participants": "<integer>"
    }
}

parser_config contains the format-specific Blueprint settings:

  • json: extraction_root, nested_loop_path, array_join_separator, and max_root_entries (reserved for a future feature; always null).
  • csv: delimiter.
  • txt: record_separator, field_separator, kv_separator, skip_header_lines, skip_footer_lines, ignore_blank_lines, and trim_whitespace.

Each entry in extraction_fields is a Relevant Field with id, scope (root or nested), expected_name, match_regex, keep_in_donation, and alias (the Rename to value).

Each entry in extraction_rules is an Extraction Rule with id, field, comparison_operator, comparison_value, and replacement_value.

Example request:

GET /ddm/api/project/KPHn7aw7/overview HTTP/1.1
Host: ddm.example.org
Authorization: Token 1176fcf7d0203db1e097861ef7442b328f1bb7f1

docs.title: Donations
docs.text:
Returns the donated data.

GET /api/project/<project-id>/donations

Parameter Required Description participants Yes Comma-separated participant IDs, for example riZVabtDI5jCpO6tvQQOTG6A,wm2tpQIFFIWaqYbgizwTif8S. blueprints No Comma-separated Blueprint IDs. If omitted, all Blueprints are returned. include_broken_test_runs No true to include test runs in which steps were skipped. Excluded by default. Header Required Description Authorization Yes Token <your-token> X-Project-Secret For projects with enhanced encryption The project password.

Response: The donations, grouped by Blueprint ID:

{
    "blueprints": {
        "<Blueprint ID>": {
            "blueprint_name": "<string>",
            "donations": [
                {
                    "participant": "<string: participant ID>",
                    "data": "<list: the extracted entries>",
                    "time_submitted": "<string: date and time (ISO 8601)>",
                    "data_extraction_state": "<string: DATA_EXTRACTED, NOT_ATTEMPTED, FAILED, or NO_DATA_EXTRACTED>",
                    "consent": "<boolean>",
                    "n_data_entries": "<integer or null>"
                }
            ]
        }
    },
    "metadata": {
        "n_blueprints": "<integer>"
    }
}

For the meaning of data_extraction_state, see Download → Participation Overview.

                    "participant": "wm2tpQIFFIWaqYbgizwTif8S",
                    "data": [
                        {"title": "Learn Python in 1 Hour", "time": "2025-01-12T20:15:00"}
                    ],
                    "time_submitted": "2025-01-15T09:16:36.456329+01:00",
                    "data_extraction_state": "DATA_EXTRACTED",
                    "consent": true,

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Returns the questionnaire responses.

GET /api/project/<project-id>/responses

Parameter Required Description participants No Comma-separated participant IDs. If omitted, the responses of all participants are returned. include_snapshot No true to include the questionnaire as each participant saw it (questionnaire_snapshot and questionnaire_config). include_broken_test_runs No true to include test runs in which steps were skipped. Excluded by default. csv No true to get a CSV file instead of JSON. Header Required Description Authorization Yes Token <your-token> X-Project-Secret For projects with enhanced encryption The project password.

Response:

{
    "responses": [
        {
            "participant": "<string: participant ID>",
            "response_data": "<object: variable name and answer pairs>",
            "time_submitted": "<string: date and time (ISO 8601)>",
            "questionnaire_complete": "<boolean: true if the participant submitted the last page>",
            "questionnaire_snapshot": "<object: only with include_snapshot=true>",
            "questionnaire_config": "<list: only with include_snapshot=true>"
        }
    ],
    "metadata": {
        "n_responses": "<integer>"
    }
}

For the answer codes -77 and -99, see Download → Download Questionnaire Responses.

Example:

GET /ddm/api/project/KPHn7aw7/responses?participants=cSCslglsu2Mv0j0ryz8lGrcA HTTP/1.1
Host: ddm.example.org
Authorization: Token 1176fcf7d0203db1e097861ef7442b328f1bb7f1

{
    "responses": [
        {
            "participant": "cSCslglsu2Mv0j0ryz8lGrcA",
            "response_data": {"media_use": "3", "media_use_reason": "-99"},

            "questionnaire_complete": true
        }
    ],
    "metadata": {"n_responses": 1}
}

docs.title: Delete Participant
docs.text:
Deletes a participant, including their donations and responses. This can't be undone.

DELETE /api/project/<project-id>/participant/<participant-id>/delete

Header Required Description Authorization Yes Token <your-token>

If the participant doesn't exist, the endpoint returns 404.

Example:

DELETE /ddm/api/project/KPHn7aw7/participant/I8RohmYJrcaCLxHP1bnEuuHn/delete HTTP/1.1
Host: ddm.example.org
Authorization: Token 1176fcf7d0203db1e097861ef7442b328f1bb7f1

{
    "message": "Participant with external id 'I8RohmYJrcaCLxHP1bnEuuHn' successfully deleted."
}

docs.title: Continuation
docs.text: After participants request their data from a platform, it can take hours or days until they can download it. With a continuation link, participants can leave the study and come back later to upload their data.

docs.title: The Continuation Link
docs.text:
Each participant has their own continuation link:

https://<your-ddm-server>/ddm/<url-identifier>/continue?p=<participant-id>

If the participant ID doesn't exist, participants see a page saying that continuation failed, with the option to start a new participation.

docs.title: Show the Link to Participants
docs.text:
Add the link to your instructions with the variable {{ participant_id }}, which DDM replaces with each participant's ID (see Dynamic Content). For example:

It can take up to a few days until you can download your data. Save this link, for
example as a bookmark or by sending it to yourself by email, and use it to continue
when your data is ready:

https://your-ddm-server.example.org/ddm/my-study/continue?p={{ participant_id }}

Ask participants to keep the link private

Anyone with a participant's continuation link can continue that participation, without logging in. Ask participants not to share it.

docs.title: Dynamic Content
docs.text:
Some texts in DDM can change depending on the participant: for example, show the participant's ID, thank only participants who donated data, or refer to the donated data in a question. You do this with template code in the text.

Template code works in these texts:

  • The briefing text.
  • The donation instructions.
  • The debriefing text and the redirect address.
  • Question and item texts. In questions linked to a Blueprint, you can also include the participant's donated data (see Data Integration).

Template code has three parts:

  • Variables insert a value: {{ participant_id }}.
  • Tags add logic, such as conditions: {% if … %} … {% endif %}.
  • Filters change a value: {{ participant_id|truncatechars:5 }}.

Always test your template code

A mistake in template code, such as a missing {% endif %} or an unsupported tag, can stop the page from loading for participants. After every change, check the page with the test link.

docs.title: Available Tags and Filters
docs.text: DDM supports only the variables, tags, and filters listed below. They work like in Django's template language, which the links describe in more detail.

docs.title: Available Variables
docs.text:
Write variables in double curly braces. For example, the text

Your participation ID is {{ participant_id }}.

is shown to participants as "Your participation ID is xHQVbrYUYXn5lklW3RGSeouX."

participant_id

The participant's ID.

url_parameter

The values of the extracted URL parameters. Add the parameter's name after a dot. For example, if the link contained ?channel=email, {{ url_parameter.channel }} shows email.

briefing_consent

Only if you ask for consent on the briefing page: "1" if the participant consented and "0" if not. These are texts, so compare them with quotes: {% if briefing_consent == "1" %}.

donation_info

Counts that describe the participant's donations. Add the count's name after a dot, for example {{ donation_info.n_consent }}:

Name Number of Blueprints… n_success from which data was extracted successfully, whether or not the participant consented. n_pending for which no extraction was attempted yet, for example because the participant didn't upload a file. n_failed for which an upload was attempted but failed. n_consent from which data was extracted and the participant consented to donate it. n_no_consent from which data was extracted but the participant declined to donate it. n_no_data_extracted for which the Extraction Rules removed all entries.

donated_data

Only in questions linked to a Blueprint: the data that this Blueprint extracted for the participant. For how it's structured and how to use it, see Data Integration.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Write tags in {% … %}. Most tags need a closing tag, such as {% endif %}. If it's missing, the text isn't shown at all.

For example, on the debriefing page:

{% if donation_info.n_consent == 0 %}
Unfortunately, you didn't donate any data.
{% else %}
Thank you very much for donating your data!
{% endif %}

Participants who donated at least some data see "Thank you very much for donating your data!".

Tag What it does {% if %} … {% elif %} … {% else %} … {% endif %} Shows text only if a condition is true. {% for %} … {% endfor %} Repeats text for each entry of a list. {% ifchanged %} … {% else %} … {% endifchanged %} In a loop, shows text only if a value differs from the previous entry. {% regroup %} Groups the entries of a list by a field.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Add filters to a variable with |. For example, {{ "abcde"|truncatechars:3 }} shows "ab…".

Filter What it does date Formats a date, for example {{ entry.time |date:"d.m.Y" }}. default Shows a fallback text if the value is empty or missing, for example {{ url_parameter.channel |default:"unknown" }}. dictsort Sorts a list by a field, for example donated_data |dictsort:"time". dictsortreversed Sorts a list by a field in reverse order. first The first entry of a list. last The last entry of a list. length The number of entries in a list, or of characters in a text. random A random entry of a list. truncatechars Shortens a text to a number of characters, including the "…". truncatewords Shortens a text to a number of words.

docs.title: Different Debriefing Texts Depending on Consent
docs.text:
To thank participants differently depending on whether they consented on the briefing page, use this debriefing text:

{% if briefing_consent == "1" %}
Thank you for taking part in this study.
{% else %}
You decided not to take part in this study. We respect your decision.
{% endif %}

Your participation ID is "{{ participant_id }}". To have your data deleted later, send this
ID to someone@example.org.

Participants who consented see:

Thank you for taking part in this study.

Your participation ID is "xHQVbrYUYXn5lklW3RGSeouX". To have your data deleted later, send this ID to someone@example.org.
